note: Track runs (voice-runs), step 2: Do Mi Sol and the high Do, one note per beat on a staff, then the book's home chord run in eighths, with its chords and alone. missing: a run-singer prop that caps the top note (its last pass puts the high Do on the top of the voice's range), and an arpeggio run the book rates under Hard (this stage holds one Hard and two Expert runs; only the Hard one is used).

exercise.title: The home chord as a quick run
exercise.why: This run skips up the notes of the home chord, so you place Do, Mi, Sol and the high Do one at a time first, and the run only asks you to move between places your voice already knows.

cells.text:
Press Start exercise below: the metronome and the mic start together, and your pitch shows as a line on the staff. Sing {{1}}, {{3}}, {{5}} from the low {{1}}, go on up to the next {{1}}, then come back down the same way, one note per beat. Sing them on the note names.
Practice until each skip lands on its click without a slide.

Press Play below to hear the run: two chords set the key, and the mic starts with them. The run skips from Do up through Mi and Sol to the high Do and back, two notes per beat. Each pass starts a semitone higher. Sing along on "ah", and take the high Do on "oo".
If the high Do feels tight, leave it out and sing the three notes under it.
_Don't reach for high notes: stop singing at the pass where the run stops feeling easy, and listen to the rest._

Press Play below to hear the run: the mic starts with it. The chords are gone now, so the run is the only sound and you find each new key from its first note. Sing along on "ah", and take the high Do on "oo".
If a pass starts off its note, listen to that pass and come in on the next one.
